symptom: `make ci-local` could not pass on a clone without submodules: TestIssue1640_RegisteredListMarkersAreWhatStudioProStores failed with `lstat ../../../testdata/testapp/TestApp/mprcontents: no such file or directory` while 125 other packages passed. The same test passes in CI, so the failure looks like something the current change broke.
cause: testdata/testapp is a git SUBMODULE (ako/TestApp, gitlink pinned at 11a8fcac) that .github/workflows/push-test.yml checks out with `submodules: true`, so CI always has it and `git clone` without --recurse-submodules does not. studioProUnits walked both fixture roots unconditionally and fed WalkDir's lstat error into t.Fatal; mdl/roundtrip already skipped the same fixture with a remedy message (skipIfMissing), so the two disagreed. A single floor of 1000 units over both roots was the second half: dropping the 900-unit submodule leaves pedapp's 369, so skipping alone would have tripped the floor instead. Fixed with per-root floors, a skip carrying the `git submodule update --init testdata/testapp` remedy, and a t.Fatal when os.Getenv("CI") is set.
insight: A test that hard-fails on an uncommitted fixture makes the project's own pre-push gate unpassable, and the cost is not the failing test — it is that a pre-existing failure becomes indistinguishable from one you just caused. The cheap discriminator is to run the single test in a clean worktree at the base commit; that settles it in one step, where reading the diff for a plausible culprit settles nothing. The fix is NOT a bare t.Skip: ako/mxcli#808 shipped green because an integration test had only ever skipped, and this census is the only thing holding canon's list-marker registrations against Studio Pro-authored documents. Skip locally, FAIL under CI (os.Getenv("CI"), as cmd/mxcli/gitstate.go already does), so the skip can never fire where coverage matters. And check the assertions downstream of the data you just made optional: the units floor would have failed the test anyway, turning one confusing failure into another.
